page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 93.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. Graphics processing is handled by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on network-attached storage, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, with single-threaded gzip compression falling into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform in the middle 50% range, though the Passmark memory score is weak. The integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for LLM prompt processing on small and medium models, and strong performance for medium-model text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a balanced resource density for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the high cost of newer-generation accelerators. The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and a Turing-architecture GPU makes this instance suitable for machine learning inference, specifically prompt processing and text generation for small to medium models. It is also appropriate for multi-threaded data processing, image processing, and ray tracing workloads that can leverage GPU acceleration alongside moderate multi-core CPU capabilities.
